1	# Carbon-aware Compute Scheduling Market
2	
3	A backend service for a carbon-aware batch-compute scheduling market. The service will evolve around scheduling and migrating batch jobs using live energy mix, regional carbon intensity, execution cost, deadlines, and data-residency constraints.
4	
5	## Run
6	
7	Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.
8	
9	```bash
10	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
11	```
12	
13	The initial public endpoint is `GET /health`, which returns JSON with `status: "ok"`.
14	
15	## Audit endpoint
16	
17	```bash
18	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --token TOKEN
19	```
20	
21	`--audit` and `--token` form a pair: both omitted leaves `GET /audit` a plain 404 like any other unknown path, while giving only one, an empty value or a repeated option is a usage error (exit status 2). When both are given, `GET /audit` serves read-only queries against the audit journal at `PATH`; clients cannot select another file.
22	
23	Requests must carry exactly one `X-Audit-Token` header whose value equals `TOKEN` (missing, blank or duplicated headers get 401, a mismatched value 403). The query string maps to `audit.search`: optional `cursor`, `limit` (a decimal integer from 1 to 1000, default 100), `op`, `stage` and `key` filters. Unknown, repeated or empty parameters get 400 `invalid_request`. A missing journal gets 404 `audit_not_found`, malformed journal content 409 `audit_invalid`, and other I/O failures 503 `audit_unavailable`.
24	
25	## Multi-token scoped authorization
26	
27	```bash
28	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --auth CONFIG
29	```
30	
31	`--auth` is an alternative to `--token`; the two are mutually exclusive, and enabling the audit endpoint requires exactly one of them (anything else is a usage error, exit status 2). `CONFIG` is a UTF-8 file whose every non-empty line is a six-element JSON array:
32	
33	```json
34	["name", "sha256-hex", grace_until, ops, stages, keys]
35	```
36	
37	- `name` — a unique non-empty label for the token.
38	- `sha256-hex` — the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the token's raw UTF-8 bytes; unique across records. The file never holds plaintext tokens.
39	- `grace_until` — `null` or a non-negative integer Unix second; the token stays valid while the current Unix second is not greater than it.
40	- `ops`, `stages`, `keys` — each either `"*"` (the filter may be omitted or take any legal value) or an array of distinct non-empty strings, in which case the request must carry that filter explicitly with a value in the array. Operation and stage scopes use the search filter domains (`copy`/`restore`; `成功`, `校验`, `执行`, `同步`, `回滚`); history keys match exactly.
41	
42	The whole file is validated at startup (any error exits with status 2 without listening) and re-read on every request, so a same-directory atomic replacement rotates tokens without a restart: add the new digest and set a grace cutoff on the old one. A configuration that cannot be read or validated after startup answers 503 `auth_unavailable`. Unknown or expired tokens get 403; a valid token whose request lacks a required in-scope filter gets 403 as well, after query-parameter validation (400) and before the audit file is ever opened.
43	
44	## Proof export endpoint
45	
46	```bash
47	python -m carbon_market serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --audit PATH --token TOKEN --checkpoint CPATH
48	```
49	
50	`--checkpoint` enables `GET /audit/proof`, the online export of `audit_proof.export` against the fixed checkpoint `CPATH`; it may only be given together with `--audit` (alone, empty or repeated it is a usage error, exit status 2). Without it the proof path stays a plain 404 like any other unknown path. Clients can never select the audit or checkpoint file through the query.
51	
52	The same authorization as `GET /audit` applies, in the same order (401/403, 400 `invalid_request`, scoped filters 403, 503 `auth_unavailable`). The query takes a mandatory non-empty `generation` name, an optional `final` flag (exactly `true` or `false`, defaulting to `false`) and the usual `cursor`, `limit`, `op`, `stage` and `key` filters. A successful export answers 200 with the offline-savable proof object, its page computed from the same journal snapshot the proof seals. The proof object is version 2 and ends with `checkpoint_etag`: the strong entity tag of the checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the SHA-256 of the complete bytes, exactly the computation and quoting the checkpoint download serves — so every proof is bound to precisely one checkpoint snapshot, and any later anchor, closing or new generation rebinds the proofs that follow it. A missing journal or checkpoint parent directory gets 404 `proof_not_found` (the real paths never leak); an invalid chain, checkpoint, generation state or growth relation gets 409 `proof_invalid` and appends no anchor; locking or I/O failures get 503 `proof_unavailable` with the old checkpoint preserved.
53	
54	## Checkpoint snapshot endpoint
55	
56	With `--checkpoint` configured, `GET /audit/checkpoint` offers the fixed checkpoint file itself as a read-only, conditionally cached download. The endpoint takes no path or query parameters: the response always comes from the one `CPATH` fixed at startup, so a client can neither select nor probe a location.
57	
58	Authorization follows the same order as the other audit endpoints: a missing, blank or duplicated `X-Audit-Token` is 401 `unauthorized`; an unknown or expired token is 403 `forbidden`; an authorization configuration that cannot be read or validated at request time is 503 `auth_unavailable` with no configuration detail in the body. A multi-token record may download only when its operation, stage and history-key scopes are all `*`; any restricted scope gets 403.
59	
60	The optional `If-None-Match` header may be omitted or appear exactly once as a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. A blank, duplicated or malformed conditional header gets 400 `invalid_request` and never opens the checkpoint; the same goes for any query string. The response on success (200) is the checkpoint's original UTF-8 bytes, served verbatim with `Content-Type: application/json` — never re-serialized — and an `ETag` that is the lowercase SHA-256 of the complete response bytes in strong-tag form (`"<64 hex>"`). When the conditional value equals the current ETag the answer is 304 with an empty body and the same ETag; otherwise it is 200 with the full bytes, and both decisions are made from one validated snapshot.
61	
62	The bytes are read under the same checkpoint lock exports use (shared), held from open through validation and ETag computation, so a request racing an export observes only a complete old or complete new version. A missing checkpoint gets 404 `checkpoint_not_found`; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 or JSON, or a checkpoint with an illegal version, field order, anchor or digest chain, get 409 `checkpoint_invalid` with a body of only `{"error":...}`; other I/O failures get 503 `checkpoint_unavailable`. Real paths and system messages never appear in an error. Without `--checkpoint` the path remains a plain 404 like any other unknown path.
63	
64	## Offline bundle verification
65	
66	```bash
67	python -m carbon_market verify-bundle --checkpoint CPATH --proof PPATH --etag ETAG
68	```
69	
70	`verify-bundle` verifies a downloaded checkpoint/proof pair entirely offline; it never touches the journal and never rewrites its inputs. All three options must appear exactly once with non-empty values, and `--etag` must be a single strong tag — one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, exactly as the download's `ETag` header carried it. Any argument or tag-format error exits with status 2 and `{"error":"invalid_request"}` on stderr before either file is read.
71	
72	Verification first recomputes the tag from the checkpoint's raw bytes — a mismatch fails immediately — then reads both files as UTF-8 JSON (negative-zero and non-finite number literals are format errors), revalidates the checkpoint's complete anchor chain, and applies the same offline proof checks as `audit_proof.verify`: embedded log bytes, query parameters, recomputed page, cursor and root digest, with the generation, anchor and closed state taken from the checkpoint snapshot in hand. The passed `--etag`, the recomputed tag and the proof's bound `checkpoint_etag` must all three agree, so an old proof against a new checkpoint, a new proof against an old checkpoint, or a tag carried by another download response is a verification failure. Proofs without the snapshot binding (version 1) are not verifiable offline and count as incomplete proof structures. Everything happens under the checkpoint's shared lock on the one snapshot that was read, so a same-directory atomic replacement racing the verification can only yield a self-consistent old or new combination, never a mix of two versions.
73	
74	On success stdout carries one compact UTF-8 JSON line — `{"valid":true,"etag":...,"generation":...,"closed":...,"events":...,"next":...}` with non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline — the exit status is 0 and stderr stays empty. Failures print no partial stdout, only a single compact failure object on stderr: status 2 `invalid_request` (argument or tag format), 3 `invalid_bundle` (encoding, JSON or structure, including proofs without the snapshot binding), 4 `verification_failed` (tag, digest chain, generation, anchor, state, page or snapshot-binding mismatch) and 5 `bundle_unavailable` (missing files or other locking, open or read errors). Failure objects never leak paths, system messages or input content.
75	
76	## Test
77	
78	```bash
79	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
80	```
81

1	"""Independent checkpoints and scope proofs over the audit journal.
2	
3	This module adds two capabilities the read-only :mod:`carbon_market.audit`
4	journal does not provide on its own: an independent checkpoint file that
5	is not the journal and an offline-savable proof of a particular search.
6	
7	:func:`export` reads the complete journal snapshot under the *same*
8	``cursor`` / ``limit`` / ``op`` / ``stage`` / ``key`` arguments
9	:func:`carbon_market.audit.search` takes and returns a version 2 proof
10	object that encapsulates the query, the result page and the journal's
11	raw bytes, together with the named generation and its closed state. The
12	proof ends with ``checkpoint_etag``: the strong entity tag of the
13	checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit -- one
14	double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the SHA-256 of
15	the complete bytes, exactly the computation and quoting the checkpoint
16	download serves -- so every proof is bound to precisely one checkpoint
17	snapshot. Each successful non-duplicate export appends one anchor to
18	the checkpoint at ``checkpoint_path``: the anchor binds
19	
20	* the complete event manifest -- every audit key paired with its event
21	  digest, in journal order;
22	* the SHA-256 of the journal's raw bytes (the *log digest*), so a log
23	  rotation that preserves the sealed events still produces a new anchor
24	  while the chain continues;
25	* the root head the journal declares;
26	* the digest of the previous anchor (null for the very first anchor of
27	  the checkpoint, so the stream stays one continuous chain across
28	  generations) and the closed flag.
29	
30	The query parameters and the returned page are not anchored: the proof
31	carries them and :func:`verify` recomputes the page from the embedded
32	journal bytes and parameters, so any tampering with log bytes,
33	parameters, page or cursor shows up as a mismatch. Exports of different
34	queries against an unchanged snapshot append no anchor; their proofs
35	name the snapshot's existing anchor.
36	
37	The anchor digest is the SHA-256 of that five-part binding serialized with the
38	journal's compact UTF-8 JSON convention, so rotating the journal bytes
39	while the sealed chain survives keeps the anchor chain continuous --
40	every anchor also commits to the previous anchor digest.
41	
42	Generations are non-empty, unique, non-regressing names (strictly
43	ascending in code-point order): a checkpoint is an ordered list of
44	generations, and a new generation can only be created once the previous
45	one is closed. Within one generation every export must
46	preserve the already anchored events key by key and digest by digest; a
47	snapshot may keep the same manifest (a re-query, or a byte-preserving
48	log rotation) or add new keys -- which may land anywhere in code-point
49	order, since the anchored pairs are compared key by key, not by
50	position -- but a deletion, a rewrite of a known event or a retreat
51	raises ``ValueError`` and appends nothing. An export
52	identical in manifest, log digest, head and closed state is a duplicate:
53	it appends no anchor and returns a proof naming that same anchor, no
54	matter which query it carried. Passing ``final=True`` closes the current
55	generation -- the closing anchor may pin the same snapshot, only its
56	closed flag flips -- and once closed only the identical idempotent
57	export (``final=True``) is accepted.
58	
59	:func:`verify` takes *only* the checkpoint path and a previously
60	exported proof -- the journal itself is never opened -- rechecks the
61	proof envelope, recomputes the strong tag of the checkpoint bytes read
62	under the lock and confronts it with the proof's bound
63	``checkpoint_etag``, recomputes the page from the embedded log bytes and
64	page, reparses the embedded journal, rechecks every anchor chain, and
65	returns the proof's original search result together with its generation
66	and closed state. Any change to the embedded log bytes, parameters, page
67	content, cursor or any digest raises ``ValueError``; a proof whose bound
68	tag does not match the checkpoint in hand -- an old proof against a new
69	checkpoint or a new proof against an old one -- mismatches as well.
70	
71	:func:`verify_bundle` is the offline entry for a downloaded pair: it
72	takes the checkpoint file, the saved proof file and the strong entity
73	tag the download carried, recomputes the tag from the checkpoint's raw
74	bytes before anything else, and then applies the same checkpoint and
75	proof validation as :func:`verify` against the single locked snapshot
76	it read, so a racing same-directory replacement can only yield a
77	self-consistent old or new combination. The passed tag, the recomputed
78	tag and the proof's bound ``checkpoint_etag`` must all three agree, so
79	a tag carried by another download response never verifies. Structural
80	failures (encoding, JSON grammar, field shapes, and version 1 proofs,
81	which predate the snapshot binding) raise ``BundleFormatError`` while
82	every tag, digest-chain, generation, anchor, closed-state, page or
83	snapshot-binding mismatch raises ``BundleMismatchError``; both are
84	public ``ValueError`` subclasses that let the command-line entry tell a
85	malformed bundle apart from a failed verification.
86	
87	Exports only accept a complete version 2 journal: a version 1 journal,
88	a broken digest chain or a malformed checkpoint structure raises
89	``ValueError``. Invalid argument types, an empty generation name, a
90	non-boolean ``final`` or out-of-range search parameters are rejected
91	with ``ValueError`` *before any file is read*. A missing audit journal,
92	a checkpoint required for verification, or a missing checkpoint parent
93	directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; every other locking or I/O
94	failure surfaces unchanged as ``OSError``.
95	
96	An export holds the journal's shared kernel flock and the checkpoint's
97	exclusive kernel flock together, and the checkpoint commits via a
98	same-directory temporary file that is written and fsynced, moved over
99	the checkpoint with :func:`os.replace` and followed by a directory
100	fsync. A commit failure therefore never leaves a new anchor behind nor
101	returns a proof; concurrent appenders serialize and each observes
102	either the complete previous checkpoint or the complete new one, and a
103	restarted process continues the same anchor chain from the persisted
104	checkpoint.
105	"""

191	@contextlib.contextmanager
192	def _file_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
193	    # Same flock discipline as the journal: the companion lock file is
194	    # never unlinked and the kernel releases the flock on process exit.
195	    lock_path = realpath + ".lock"
196	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
197	    try:
198	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
199	        try:
200	            yield
201	        finally:
202	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
203	    finally:
204	        os.close(fd)

207	def _is_digest(value: object) -> bool:
208	    return isinstance(value, str) and len(value) == 64 \

212	def _compact(payload: Any) -> bytes:
213	    # The journal's compact UTF-8 JSON convention: compact separators,
214	    # non-ASCII written through. Used for every digest here.
215	    return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
216	                      allow_nan=False).encode("utf-8")

219	def _strong_tag(raw: bytes) -> str:
220	    # The strong entity tag of a checkpoint snapshot: one double-quoted
221	    # string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the SHA-256 of the
222	    # complete bytes -- exactly the computation and quoting the
223	    # conditional download serves in its ETag header.
224	    return '"' + hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() + '"'

228	                   head: str | None, previous: str | None,
229	                   closed: bool) -> str:
230	    return hashlib.sha256(_compact(
231	        [manifest, log_digest, head, previous, closed])).hexdigest()

258	def _manifest(document: dict[str, Any]) -> list[list[Any]]:
259	    # The complete snapshot inventory: every audit key in journal order
260	    # paired with the exact digest its sealed chain gives it. Comparing
261	    # manifests item by item enforces "known events unchanged, only new
262	    # keys added" without trusting the journal bytes alone.
263	    chain = document["chain"]
264	    return [[audit_key, chain[audit_key][1]]
265	            for audit_key in document["events"]]

268	def _validate_manifest(raw: object) -> list[list[Any]]:
269	    if not isinstance(raw, list):
270	        raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest must be a list of "
271	                                "[audit key, event digest] pairs")
272	    manifest: list[list[Any]] = []
273	    last_key: str | None = None
274	    for item in raw:
275	        if not isinstance(item, list) or len(item) != 2 \
276	                or not isinstance(item[0], str) or not item[0] \
277	                or not _is_digest(item[1]):
278	            raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest entries must be "
279	                                    "[non-empty key, 64-digit hex digest]")
280	        if last_key is not None and item[0] <= last_key:
281	            raise BundleFormatError("anchor manifest must be ordered by "
282	                                    "key code point without repeats")
283	        manifest.append([item[0], item[1]])
284	        last_key = item[0]
285	    return manifest

288	def _check_extension(old_manifest: list[list[Any]],
289	                     new_manifest: list[list[Any]]) -> None:
290	    # The old snapshot must survive key by key: every anchored key keeps
291	    # its exact digest, while new keys may land anywhere in code-point
292	    # order -- the manifests are compared as key/digest pairs, not by
293	    # position. Fewer entries (retreat), a missing old key (deletion) or
294	    # a changed digest under a known key (rewrite) all surface here.
295	    # Equal manifests (re-query or byte-level log rotation with same
296	    # events) are permitted by the caller and never reach this check.
297	    if len(new_manifest) <= len(old_manifest):
298	        raise BundleMismatchError("a generation only accepts snapshots "
299	                                  "that add new audit events")
300	    new_digests = {audit_key: digest for audit_key, digest in new_manifest}
301	    for audit_key, digest in old_manifest:
302	        if new_digests.get(audit_key) != digest:
303	            raise BundleMismatchError("a generation cannot rewrite, delete "
304	                                      "or reorder an already anchored event")
305	
306	
307	def _validate_checkpoint(data: object) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
308	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or list(data.keys()) != list(_ROOT_FIELDS):
309	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint root must be an object with "
310	                                "keys version and generations, in that "
311	                                "order")
312	    version = data["version"]
313	    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) \
314	            or version != _CHECKPOINT_VERSION:
315	        raise BundleFormatError("unsupported checkpoint version")
316	    generations_raw = data["generations"]
317	    if not isinstance(generations_raw, list):
318	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint generations must be a list")
319	    if not generations_raw:
320	        # export only creates a checkpoint together with its first
321	        # generation, so a persisted empty list is structural damage.
322	        raise BundleFormatError("checkpoint must carry at least one "
323	                                "generation")
324	
325	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
326	    generations: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
327	    # The previous-anchor chain runs across the whole checkpoint: the
328	    # first anchor of a later generation names the last anchor of the
329	    # closed previous generation, so the stream never forks.
330	    previous: str | None = None
331	    for gen_position, generation_raw in enumerate(generations_raw):
332	        is_last_generation = gen_position == len(generations_raw) - 1
333	        if not isinstance(generation_raw, dict) \
334	                or list(generation_raw.keys()) != list(_GENERATION_FIELDS):
335	            raise BundleFormatError("each generation must be an object "
336	                                    "with keys name and anchors, in that "
337	                                    "order")
338	        name = generation_raw["name"]
339	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
340	            raise BundleFormatError("generation name must be a non-empty "
341	                                    "string")
342	        if name in seen_names:
343	            raise BundleFormatError("generation names must not repeat")
344	        if generations and name <= generations[-1]["name"]:
345	            # Names open in strictly ascending code-point order; an
346	            # equal-or-earlier name is a repeat or a regression.
347	            raise BundleFormatError("generation names must not regress")
348	        seen_names.add(name)
349	        anchors_raw = generation_raw["anchors"]
350	        if not isinstance(anchors_raw, list) or not anchors_raw:
351	            raise BundleFormatError("each generation must carry at least "
352	                                    "one anchor")
353	
354	        anchors: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
355	        for index, anchor_raw in enumerate(anchors_raw):
356	            is_last_anchor = index == len(anchors_raw) - 1
357	            if not isinstance(anchor_raw, dict) \
358	                    or list(anchor_raw.keys()) != list(_ANCHOR_FIELDS):
359	                raise BundleFormatError(
360	                    "each anchor must be an object with keys manifest, "
361	                    "log_digest, head, previous, closed and digest, in "
362	                    "that order")
363	            manifest = _validate_manifest(anchor_raw["manifest"])
364	            if not _is_digest(anchor_raw["log_digest"]):
365	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor log_digest must be a "
366	                                        "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal "
367	                                        "digest")
368	            head = anchor_raw["head"]
369	            if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
370	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor head must be null or a "
371	                                        "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal "
372	                                        "digest")
373	            declared_previous = anchor_raw["previous"]
374	            if index > 0 and not _is_digest(declared_previous):
375	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor previous digest must be a "
376	                                        "64-digit hexadecimal digest")
377	            if declared_previous != previous:
378	                raise BundleMismatchError("anchor previous digest does not "
379	                                          "continue the chain")
380	            if not isinstance(anchor_raw["closed"], bool):
381	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor closed must be a boolean")
382	            digest = anchor_raw["digest"]
383	            if not _is_digest(digest):
384	                raise BundleFormatError("anchor digest must be a 64-digit "
385	                                        "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
386	            expected = _anchor_digest(manifest, anchor_raw["log_digest"],
387	                                      head, previous, anchor_raw["closed"])
388	            if digest != expected:
389	                raise BundleMismatchError("anchor digest does not match "
390	                                          "its content")
391	
392	            if anchors:
393	                earlier = anchors[-1]
394	                if earlier["closed"]:
395	                    raise BundleMismatchError("a closed anchor cannot be "
396	                                              "followed inside its "
397	                                              "generation")
398	                # Consecutive anchors either pin the same manifest (a
399	                # byte-level log rotation with the events intact, or the
400	                # closing anchor flipping the closed flag) or extend it
401	                # with new keys anywhere in code-point order while every
402	                # anchored pair survives; anything else is a rewrite.
403	                if manifest == earlier["manifest"]:
404	                    if head != earlier["head"]:
405	                        raise BundleMismatchError(
406	                            "a same-snapshot anchor cannot move the root "
407	                            "digest")
408	                    if anchor_raw["log_digest"] == earlier["log_digest"] \
409	                            and anchor_raw["closed"] == earlier["closed"]:
410	                        raise BundleMismatchError("a duplicate anchor "
411	                                                  "changes nothing")
412	                else:
413	                    _check_extension(earlier["manifest"], manifest)
414	            if anchor_raw["closed"] and not is_last_anchor:
415	                raise BundleMismatchError("only the last anchor of a "
416	                                          "generation may be closed")
417	
418	            anchor = {"manifest": manifest,
419	                      "log_digest": anchor_raw["log_digest"], "head": head,
420	                      "previous": declared_previous,
421	                      "closed": anchor_raw["closed"], "digest": digest}
422	            anchors.append(anchor)
423	            previous = digest
424	
425	        if not is_last_generation and not anchors[-1]["closed"]:
426	            # An open generation may only be the last one of the
427	            # checkpoint: any following generation proves it was closed.
428	            raise BundleMismatchError("a new generation can only start "
429	                                      "after the previous one is closed")
430	        generations.append({"name": name, "anchors": anchors})
431	    return generations

434	def _parse_checkpoint(realpath: str, raw: bytes) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:

437	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
438	        raise BundleFormatError(
439	            f"checkpoint file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
440	    try:
441	        data = strict_loads(text)
442	    except ValueError as exc:

464	def _fsync_dir(directory: str) -> None:
465	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
466	    try:
467	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
468	    finally:
469	        os.close(dir_fd)

471	
472	def _commit_checkpoint(realpath: str, directory: str, payload: bytes,
473	                       old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
474	    # Same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace, directory fsync --
475	    # with a rollback if anything fails after the replace, so a failed
476	    # commit never leaves the new anchor behind. The pre-call bytes are
477	    # staged back over the file (or the file removed when it did not
478	    # exist) and the directory synced again, all while the exclusive
479	    # lock is held; a failed rollback surfaces chained after the first
480	    # error.
481	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
482	        dir=directory, prefix=".audit-proof-", suffix=".tmp")
483	    try:
484	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
485	            handle.write(payload)
486	            handle.flush()
487	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
488	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
489	    except BaseException as first:
490	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
491	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
492	        raise
493	    try:
494	        _fsync_dir(directory)
495	    except BaseException as first:
496	        audit._rollback(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
497	        raise

505	    if document["version"] != 2:
506	        raise ValueError("proof export requires a sealed version 2 audit "
507	                         "journal with a complete digest chain")

531	def export(
532	    audit_path: str,
533	    checkpoint_path: str,
534	    generation: str,
535	    final: bool = False,
536	    cursor: str | None = None,
537	    limit: int = audit._DEFAULT_LIMIT,
538	    op: str | None = None,
539	    stage: str | None = None,
540	    key: str | None = None,
541	) -> dict[str, Any]:
542	    """Export a verifiable proof and anchor it in the checkpoint.
543	
544	    ``audit_path`` and ``checkpoint_path`` must be non-empty strings;
545	    ``generation`` must be a non-empty string and ``final`` a boolean.
546	    The search arguments follow :func:`carbon_market.audit.search`. All
547	    argument errors raise ``ValueError`` before any file is read.
548	
549	    A missing audit journal raises ``FileNotFoundError``; so does a
550	    missing parent directory of a checkpoint that must be created. A
551	    version 1 journal, an incomplete digest chain, a malformed
552	    checkpoint, a repeated generation name or an export that reopens a
553	    past generation, an attempt to open a new generation while the
554	    previous one is still open, an export that deletes or rewrites
555	    events of the current generation, or any non-identical export of a
556	    closed generation raises ``ValueError``. Remaining locking or I/O
557	    failures raise ``OSError``.
558	
559	    Returns the offline proof dict: a version 2 envelope whose last
560	    field, ``checkpoint_etag``, is the strong entity tag of the
561	    checkpoint's raw bytes after this export's anchor commit -- the same
562	    quoted SHA-256 the checkpoint download serves. A repeat of an export
563	    whose content and closed state are identical appends nothing and
564	    returns a proof naming the same anchor and the unchanged snapshot's
565	    tag. With ``final=True`` the appended anchor closes
566	    generation -- it may pin the same snapshot -- after which only the
567	    identical idempotent export (``final=True``) is accepted.
568	    """
569	    for value in (audit_path, checkpoint_path):
570	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
571	            raise ValueError("audit_path and checkpoint_path must be "
572	                             "non-empty strings")
573	    if not isinstance(generation, str) or not generation:
574	        raise ValueError("generation must be a non-empty string")
575	    if not isinstance(final, bool):
576	        raise ValueError("final must be a boolean")
577	    _check_params(cursor, limit, op, stage, key)
578	
579	    audit_real = os.path.realpath(audit_path)
580	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
581	    checkpoint_store = _get_store(checkpoint_real)
582	    with checkpoint_store.lock:
583	        # Hold the journal's shared lock and the checkpoint's exclusive
584	        # lock together until the commit lands, so audit.record cannot
585	        # rotate the journal while its bytes are sealed into an anchor.
586	        with audit._file_lock(audit_real, shared=True):
587	            # Read inside the shared flock exactly like the read-only
588	            # audit queries: a racing audit.record is observed as one
589	            # complete document or the other, never a half-replaced
590	            # file. A missing journal surfaces as FileNotFoundError.
591	            with open(audit_real, "rb") as handle:
592	                raw = handle.read()
593	            document = _parse_journal_snapshot(audit_real, raw)
594	            with _file_lock(checkpoint_real):
595	                generations, old_bytes = _read_checkpoint(checkpoint_real)
596	                if generations is None:
597	                    generations = []
598	
599	                params = _params_dict(cursor, limit, op, stage, key)
600	                # Compute the page from the exact bytes in hand; this is
601	                # the same filter/pagination audit.search applies.
602	                result = _search_document(document, params)
603	                manifest = _manifest(document)
604	                head = document["head"]
605	                log_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
606	                names = [item["name"] for item in generations]
607	
608	                def identical(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
609	                    return (item["manifest"] == manifest
610	                            and item["log_digest"] == log_digest
611	                            and item["head"] == head)
612	
613	                if generation in names:
614	                    position = names.index(generation)
615	                    if position != len(generations) - 1:
616	                        # A past generation can never be reopened.
617	                        raise ValueError("a past generation cannot be "
618	                                         "exported again")
619	                    current = generations[position]
620	                    anchors = current["anchors"]
621	                    last = anchors[-1]
622	
623	                    if last["closed"]:
624	                        # Once closed the only accepted export is the
625	                        # idempotent one: final stays true and the
626	                        # snapshot is byte-for-byte the same -- events,
627	                        # log bytes and root head. The query may differ,
628	                        # since verify recomputes the page from the
629	                        # embedded log and parameters.
630	                        if not final or not identical(last):
631	                            raise ValueError("a closed generation only "
632	                                             "accepts the identical "
633	                                             "idempotent export")
634	                        return _build_proof(
635	                            generation, params, result, raw, log_digest,
636	                            head, True, last["digest"],
637	                            _strong_tag(old_bytes))
638	
639	                    # Still open. Same events, same bytes, same head and
640	                    # not closing: the duplicate export appends nothing
641	                    # and returns the proof of the latest anchor. The
642	                    # manifest must equal the latest anchor's, so an
643	                    # older snapshot cannot mask a retreat.
644	                    if not final and manifest == last["manifest"] \
645	                            and identical(last):
646	                        return _build_proof(
647	                            generation, params, result, raw, log_digest,
648	                            head, False, last["digest"],
649	                            _strong_tag(old_bytes))
650	
651	                    # Otherwise append: the manifest grows (strict
652	                    # extension), stays identical with rotated log
653	                    # bytes, or stays identical while final flips the
654	                    # closed flag. A smaller or rewritten manifest is
655	                    # rejected.
656	                    if manifest != last["manifest"]:
657	                        _check_extension(last["manifest"], manifest)
658	                    new_anchor = _make_anchor(manifest, log_digest, head,
659	                                              last["digest"], final)
660	                    anchors.append(new_anchor)
661	                else:
662	                    if generations and not \
663	                            generations[-1]["anchors"][-1]["closed"]:
664	                        raise ValueError("a new generation can only be "
665	                                         "started after the previous one "
666	                                         "is closed")
667	                    if generations and generation <= generations[-1]["name"]:
668	                        raise ValueError("generation names must not "
669	                                         "regress")
670	                    previous_digest = (
671	                        None if not generations
672	                        else generations[-1]["anchors"][-1]["digest"])
673	                    new_anchor = _make_anchor(manifest, log_digest, head,
674	                                              previous_digest, final)
675	                    generations.append(
676	                        {"name": generation, "anchors": [new_anchor]})
677	
678	                payload = _serialize_checkpoint(generations)
679	                _commit_checkpoint(
680	                    checkpoint_real,
681	                    os.path.dirname(checkpoint_real) or ".",
682	                    payload, old_bytes)
683	                # The proof binds the snapshot just committed: while the
684	                # exclusive lock is held the on-disk bytes are exactly
685	                # the committed payload, so its tag is the one a
686	                # download of this checkpoint would serve.
687	                return _build_proof(generation, params, result, raw,
688	                                    log_digest, head, final,
689	                                    new_anchor["digest"],
690	                                    _strong_tag(payload))

693	def _validate_proof(data: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
694	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or list(data.keys()) != list(_PROOF_FIELDS):
695	        raise BundleFormatError("proof must be an object with the "
696	                                "exported fields in their original order")
697	    if not isinstance(data["version"], int) \
698	            or isinstance(data["version"], bool) \
699	            or data["version"] != _PROOF_VERSION:
700	        # A version 1 proof predates the checkpoint snapshot binding and
701	        # is treated as an incomplete proof structure, never as a
702	        # mismatch.
703	        raise BundleFormatError("unsupported proof version")
704	    if not isinstance(data["generation"], str) or not data["generation"]:
705	        raise BundleFormatError("proof generation must be a non-empty "
706	                                "string")
707	    params = data["params"]
708	    if not isinstance(params, dict) \
709	            or list(params.keys()) != list(_PARAM_FIELDS):
710	        raise BundleFormatError("proof params must be the exported query "
711	                                "parameters")
712	    try:
713	        _check_params(params["cursor"], params["limit"], params["op"],
714	                      params["stage"], params["key"])
715	    except ValueError as exc:
716	        raise BundleFormatError(str(exc)) from exc
717	    result = data["result"]
718	    if not isinstance(result, dict) \
719	            or list(result.keys()) != ["events", "next"]:
720	        raise BundleFormatError("proof result must be the exported search "
721	                                "result")
722	    if not isinstance(result["events"], list):
723	        raise BundleFormatError("proof result events must be a list")
724	    next_cursor = result["next"]
725	    if next_cursor is not None and (not isinstance(next_cursor, str)
726	                                    or not next_cursor):
727	        raise BundleFormatError("proof result next must be null or a "
728	                                "non-empty string")
729	    if not isinstance(data["log_bytes"], str):
730	        raise BundleFormatError("proof log_bytes must be a string")
731	    if not _is_digest(data["log_digest"]):
732	        raise BundleFormatError("proof log_digest must be a 64-digit "
733	                                "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
734	    head = data["head"]
735	    if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
736	        raise BundleFormatError("proof head must be null or a 64-digit "
737	                                "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
738	    if not isinstance(data["closed"], bool):
739	        raise BundleFormatError("proof closed must be a boolean")
740	    if not _is_digest(data["anchor_digest"]):
741	        raise BundleFormatError("proof anchor_digest must be a 64-digit "
742	                                "lowercase hexadecimal digest")

744	    if not isinstance(checkpoint_etag, str) \
745	            or not _ETAG_RE.fullmatch(checkpoint_etag):
746	        raise BundleFormatError("proof checkpoint_etag must be a single "
747	                                "strong tag: a quoted 64-digit lowercase "
748	                                "hexadecimal digest")

752	def _search_document(document: dict[str, Any], params: dict[str, Any]) \
753	        -> dict[str, Any]:
754	    # Recompute audit.search's result from an in-memory document so
755	    # verify never needs the journal file itself.
756	    cursor = params["cursor"]
757	    limit = params["limit"]
758	    matches: list[list[Any]] = []
759	    for audit_key, event in document["events"].items():
760	        if cursor is not None and audit_key <= cursor:
761	            continue
762	        if not audit._matches(event, params["op"], params["stage"],
763	                              params["key"]):
764	            continue
765	        matches.append([audit_key, dict(event)])
766	        if len(matches) > limit:
767	            break
768	    if len(matches) > limit:
769	        page = matches[:limit]
770	        return {"events": page, "next": page[-1][0]}
771	    return {"events": matches, "next": None}

774	def _verify_proof(generations: list[dict[str, Any]],
775	                  clean: dict[str, Any],
776	                  checkpoint_real: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
777	    # The cross-checks every verified proof must pass against one
778	    # checkpoint snapshot: the named generation and anchor must be
779	    # recorded, the embedded log bytes must hash to the anchored log
780	    # digest and reparse as a sealed version 2 journal whose manifest
781	    # and root head the anchor pins, and the page must recompute from
782	    # the embedded log and parameters. Every failure here is a
783	    # mismatch, never a format error.
784	    names = [item["name"] for item in generations]
785	    if clean["generation"] not in names:
786	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof generation is not recorded in "
787	                                  "the checkpoint")
788	    generation = generations[names.index(clean["generation"])]
789	    anchor = next((item for item in generation["anchors"]
790	                   if item["digest"] == clean["anchor_digest"]), None)
791	    if anchor is None:
792	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof anchor is not recorded in the "
793	                                  "checkpoint")
794	
795	    params = clean["params"]
796	    raw = clean["log_bytes"].encode("utf-8")
797	    if hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() != clean["log_digest"]:
798	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof log bytes do not match their "
799	                                  "log digest")
800	    if clean["log_digest"] != anchor["log_digest"]:
801	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof log digest is not bound to the "
802	                                  "anchor")
803	    try:
804	        document = audit._parse_document(checkpoint_real, raw)
805	        audit._ensure_chain(document)
806	    except ValueError as exc:
807	        raise BundleMismatchError(str(exc)) from exc
808	    if document["version"] != 2:
809	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof requires a sealed version 2 "
810	                                  "audit journal")
811	    if clean["head"] != document["head"] \
812	            or anchor["head"] != document["head"]:
813	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof root digest does not match the "
814	                                  "journal")
815	    if _manifest(document) != anchor["manifest"]:
816	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof event manifest does not match "
817	                                  "the anchor")
818	    if clean["closed"] != anchor["closed"]:
819	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof closed state does not match "
820	                                  "the anchor")
821	
822	    recomputed = _search_document(document, params)
823	    if recomputed != clean["result"]:
824	        raise BundleMismatchError("proof result does not follow from "
825	                                  "the embedded log and parameters")
826	    return {"events": clean["result"]["events"],
827	            "next": clean["result"]["next"],
828	            "generation": clean["generation"],
829	            "closed": anchor["closed"]}

832	def verify(checkpoint_path: str, proof: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
833	    """Verify an exported proof solely against the checkpoint.
834	
835	    The journal is not opened: the proof carries the journal's raw
836	    bytes, parameters and result. ``checkpoint_path`` must be a
837	    non-empty string and ``proof`` an object previously returned by
838	    :func:`export`.
839	
840	    The checkpoint bytes are read under the shared lock and their
841	    strong tag is recomputed and confronted with the proof's bound
842	    ``checkpoint_etag`` before anything else: a proof exported against
843	    another snapshot -- older or newer -- mismatches. The embedded log
844	    bytes must hash to the proof's log digest, parse as
845	    a complete version 2 journal whose event manifest and root head
846	    match the anchor the proof names in the named generation of the
847	    checkpoint, and the page must recompute from the embedded log and
848	    parameters. Every anchor chain in the checkpoint is rechecked as
849	    well. Success returns
850	    ``{"events": ..., "next": ..., "generation": ..., "closed": ...}``
851	    -- the original search result together with its generation and
852	    closed state.
853	
854	    A missing checkpoint raises ``FileNotFoundError``; a proof without
855	    the snapshot binding (version 1) or any other structural problem
856	    raises ``BundleFormatError``; any proof or checkpoint mismatch --
857	    including changed log bytes, parameters, page content, cursor, any
858	    digest or a stale snapshot tag -- raises ``BundleMismatchError``;
859	    other I/O failures raise ``OSError``. Both error types are
860	    ``ValueError`` subclasses.
861	    """
862	    if not isinstance(checkpoint_path, str) or not checkpoint_path:
863	        raise ValueError("checkpoint_path must be a non-empty string")
864	
865	    clean = _validate_proof(proof)
866	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
867	    with _file_lock(checkpoint_real, shared=True):
868	        # One locked snapshot: the tag is recomputed from the exact
869	        # bytes that are then parsed and validated, so a racing
870	        # replacement can only yield a self-consistent outcome.
871	        try:
872	            with open(checkpoint_real, "rb") as handle:
873	                raw = handle.read()
874	        except FileNotFoundError:
875	            raise FileNotFoundError(
876	                f"checkpoint file {checkpoint_real!r} does not exist"
877	            ) from None
878	        if clean["checkpoint_etag"] != _strong_tag(raw):
879	            raise BundleMismatchError(
880	                "proof checkpoint_etag does not bind the checkpoint "
881	                "snapshot in hand")
882	        generations = _parse_checkpoint(checkpoint_real, raw)
883	    return _verify_proof(generations, clean, checkpoint_real)

886	def _loads_bundle(raw: bytes) -> Any:
887	    # Both downloaded files are UTF-8 JSON; a decoding failure, a
888	    # negative-zero or non-finite number literal, or a JSON grammar
889	    # error is a format error of the bundle, never a mismatch.
890	    try:
891	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
892	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
893	        raise BundleFormatError("bundle file is not valid UTF-8") from exc
894	    try:
895	        return finite_loads(text)
896	    except ValueError as exc:
897	        raise BundleFormatError("bundle file is not valid JSON") from exc
898

900	def verify_bundle(checkpoint_path: str, proof_path: str,
901	                  etag: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
902	    """Verify a downloaded checkpoint/proof pair entirely offline.
903	
904	    ``checkpoint_path`` and ``proof_path`` must be non-empty strings and
905	    ``etag`` a single strong entity tag -- one double-quoted string of
906	    64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, exactly as the checkpoint
907	    download's ``ETag`` header carried it. Argument errors raise
908	    ``ValueError`` before any file is read.
909	
910	    The checkpoint is opened, read, hashed, parsed and structurally
911	    validated under the *same* shared kernel flock an export or a
912	    download serializes against, and the whole verification runs on
913	    that one snapshot: a same-directory atomic replacement racing the
914	    read is observed as either the complete old combination or the
915	    complete new one, never a mix of two versions. The tag is
916	    recomputed from the raw checkpoint bytes first and a mismatch fails
917	    immediately, before any further parsing. The proof file is then
918	    read under the same lock and both files are checked as UTF-8 JSON
919	    (negative-zero and non-finite number literals are format errors),
920	    the checkpoint passes the complete anchor-chain validation, and the
921	    proof passes the same offline checks :func:`verify` applies --
922	    embedded log bytes, query parameters, recomputed page, cursor and
923	    root digest, with the generation, anchor and closed state taken
924	    from the checkpoint snapshot in hand. The passed tag, the
925	    recomputed tag and the proof's bound ``checkpoint_etag`` must all
926	    three agree: an old proof against a new checkpoint, a new proof
927	    against an old checkpoint or a tag carried by another download
928	    response is a mismatch. Nothing is rewritten.
929	
930	    Returns the same result dict as :func:`verify`. A missing file
931	    raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an encoding, JSON or structural error
932	    in either file -- including a version 1 proof, which predates the
933	    snapshot binding -- raises ``BundleFormatError``; a tag,
934	    digest-chain, generation, anchor, closed-state, page or
935	    snapshot-binding mismatch raises ``BundleMismatchError``; every
936	    other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. Both error types
937	    are ``ValueError`` subclasses.
938	    """
939	    for value in (checkpoint_path, proof_path):
940	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
941	            raise ValueError("checkpoint_path and proof_path must be "
942	                             "non-empty strings")
943	    if not isinstance(etag, str) or not _ETAG_RE.fullmatch(etag):
944	        raise ValueError("etag must be a single strong tag: a quoted "
945	                         "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal digest")
946	
947	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
948	    proof_real = os.path.realpath(proof_path)
949	    with _file_lock(checkpoint_real, shared=True):
950	        # One locked section for the whole bundle: the bytes whose tag
951	        # is recomputed are the bytes that are parsed, and the proof is
952	        # checked against that same snapshot.
953	        with open(checkpoint_real, "rb") as handle:
954	            raw = handle.read()
955	        tag = _strong_tag(raw)
956	        if etag != tag:
957	            raise BundleMismatchError("checkpoint bytes do not match "
958	                                      "the etag")
959	        generations = _validate_checkpoint(_loads_bundle(raw))
960	        with open(proof_real, "rb") as handle:
961	            proof_raw = handle.read()
962	        clean = _validate_proof(_loads_bundle(proof_raw))
963	        if clean["checkpoint_etag"] != tag:
964	            raise BundleMismatchError(
965	                "proof checkpoint_etag does not bind the checkpoint "
966	                "snapshot in hand")
967	        return _verify_proof(generations, clean, checkpoint_real)
968

970	def read_snapshot(checkpoint_path: str) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
971	    """Read the fixed checkpoint for a conditional, read-only download.
972	
973	    The checkpoint is opened under the *same* shared kernel flock an
974	    export uses, so a concurrent exporter serializes against the read
975	    and the caller observes either the complete old file or the
976	    complete new one, never a half-replaced document. The raw bytes are
977	    read, decoded as UTF-8, parsed and structurally validated -- the
978	    whole anchor/digest chain included -- and the SHA-256 of the exact
979	    response bytes is computed, all while the shared lock is held. The
980	    bytes themselves are returned untouched: the caller serves them
981	    verbatim, never re-serialized.
982	
983	    ``checkpoint_path`` must be a non-empty string (a bad argument
984	    raises ``ValueError`` before any file is read). A missing
985	    checkpoint raises ``FileNotFoundError``; bytes that are not valid
986	    UTF-8 or JSON, or a checkpoint whose version, field order,
987	    generation names, anchors or digest chain do not validate, raise
988	    ``ValueError``; every other locking or I/O failure raises
989	    ``OSError``.
990	    """
991	    if not isinstance(checkpoint_path, str) or not checkpoint_path:
992	        raise ValueError("checkpoint_path must be a non-empty string")
993	
994	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
995	    with _file_lock(checkpoint_real, shared=True):
996	        # Open, read, validate and hash under one shared lock: the
997	        # bytes the ETag summarizes are the validated bytes and both
998	        # come from the same complete file version.
999	        with open(checkpoint_real, "rb") as handle:
1000	            raw = handle.read()
1001	        try:
1002	            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
1003	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
1004	            raise BundleFormatError(
1005	                f"checkpoint file {checkpoint_real!r} is not valid UTF-8"
1006	            ) from exc
1007	        try:
1008	            data = strict_loads(text)
1009	        except ValueError as exc:
1010	            raise BundleFormatError(
1011	                f"checkpoint file {checkpoint_real!r} is not valid JSON"
1012	            ) from exc
1013	        _validate_checkpoint(data)
1014	        etag = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
1015	    return raw, etag
